He published more poetry before the outbreak of the [Franco-Prussian War](/wiki/Franco-Prussian_War "Franco-Prussian War"). This war, which he discussed in *Impressions de la guerre* (1872) and *La France* (1874), permanently damaged his health.

During his career, Prudhomme gradually shifted from the sentimental style of his first books towards a more personal style which unified the formality of the [Parnassus](/wiki/Parnassianism "Parnassianism") school with his interest in philosophical and scientific subjects. One of his inspirations was clearly [Lucretius](/wiki/Lucretius "Lucretius")'s *[De rerum natura](/wiki/De_rerum_natura "De rerum natura")*, whose first book he translated into verse. His philosophy was expressed in *La Justice* (1878) and *Le Bonheur* (1888). The extreme economy of means employed in these poems has, however, usually been judged as compromising their poetical quality without advancing their claims as works of philosophy. He was elected to the [Académie française](/wiki/Acad%C3%A9mie_fran%C3%A7aise "Académie française") in 1881. Another distinction, *Chevalier de la [Légion d’honneur](/wiki/L%C3%A9gion_d%E2%80%99honneur "Légion d’honneur")*, was to follow in 1895.

After *Le Bonheur*, Prudhomme turned from poetry to write essays on [aesthetics](/wiki/Aesthetics "Aesthetics") and philosophy. By 1941 the conflict had become a stalemate. Although Japan had occupied much of northern, central, and coastal China, the [Nationalist Government](/wiki/Nationalist_Government "Nationalist Government") had retreated to the interior and set up a provisional capital at [Chongqing](/wiki/Chongqing "Chongqing"), while the [Chinese communists](/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") remained in control of base areas in [Shaanxi](/wiki/Shaanxi "Shaanxi"). Japanese offensive action against the retreating and regrouping Chinese forces was largely stalled by the mountainous terrain in southwestern China, while the Communists organized widespread [guerrilla](/wiki/Guerrilla_warfare "Guerrilla warfare") and saboteur activities in northern and eastern China behind the Japanese front line.

Japan sponsored several [puppet governments](/wiki/Puppet_government "Puppet government"), one of which was headed by [Wang Jingwei](/wiki/Wang_Jingwei "Wang Jingwei").[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJansen2002636-72) Conflicts between Chinese Communist and Nationalist forces vying for territorial control behind enemy lines [culminated in a major armed clash in January 1941](/wiki/New_Fourth_Army_Incident "New Fourth Army Incident"), effectively ending their co-operation.[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFairbankGoldman1994320-73)

Japanese [strategic bombing](/wiki/Strategic_bombing_during_World_War_II "Strategic bombing during World War II") efforts mostly targeted large Chinese cities such as Shanghai, [Wuhan](/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan"), and [Chongqing](/wiki/Bombing_of_Chongqing "Bombing of Chongqing"), with around 5,000 raids from February 1938 to August 1943. Originally Albrechts University, the university started with four faculties (theology, philosophy, medicine, and law). Its establishment belongs to the second wave of university foundings in the German-speaking world in the late [Middle Ages](/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), like the [University of Tübingen](/wiki/University_of_T%C3%BCbingen "University of Tübingen") and the [University of Basel](/wiki/University_of_Basel "University of Basel") ([Switzerland](/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland")). Established by papal privilege ([papal bull](/wiki/Papal_bull "Papal bull")), the university in Freiburg actually was – like all or most universities in the Middle Ages – a corporation of the church body and therefore belonged to the [Roman Catholic Church](/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church "Roman Catholic Church") and its hierarchy. The bishop of [Basel](/wiki/Basel "Basel") consequently was its [provost](/wiki/Provost_(education) "Provost (education)") or [chancellor](/wiki/Chancellor "Chancellor") (*Kanzler*), the bishop of [Constance](/wiki/Konstanz "Konstanz") was its patron, and the real founder of the university was the sovereign, Archduke [Albert VI of Austria](/wiki/Albert_VI_of_Austria "Albert VI of Austria"), being the brother of [Frederick III](/wiki/Frederick_III,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor"), Emperor of the [Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation](/wiki/Holy_Roman_Empire_of_the_German_Nation "Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation").
